newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-KPN mulls sale of TNT non-core assets.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-KPN mulls sale of TNT non-core assets.

text.p: Dutch telecom and postal group Koninklijke PTT Nederland NV (KPN) said on Wednesday it would review over the next year or so whether to keep TNT Ltd units that were not involved in the time-sensitive freight and logistics businesses.
TNT's major non-core businesses include its general operations in Australia and its 50 percent stake in airline leasing business Ansett Worldwide, which it owns jointly with News Corp Ltd.

"We will, as we've expressed, aim to be the leader in the time sensitive distribution and logistics business and anything that does not fit into that we will review," KPN chief executive Wim Dik told a news conference.
He had been asked if KPN would sell non-core assets like TNT's Australian general freight business and Ansett Worldwide.
He said the review would be carried out over the next year and KPN had yet to form a view.

Earlier on Wednesday, KPN launched a A$2.45 per share cash takeover bid for TNT that valued the transport and logistics group at A$2.0 billion, 50 percent above TNT's previous share price and market capitalisation.
TNT's board recommended shareholders accept the bid and brokers have said it is likely to be successful.
